explanation: A fruit is a mature ovary. Fruits are classified by their development: 1) Simple fruits: derive from a single ovary, which may contain one or several chambers. 2) Compound fruits: develop from multiple ovaries. These include aggregate fruits (multiple ovaries from a single flower on one receptacle, e.g., blackberry) and multiple fruits (ovaries from separate flowers clustered together in an inflorescence, e.g., pineapple).

questions.q: What type of fruit is a blackberry, and how does it develop?
opts: Simple fruit; from a single ovary with one chamber
Aggregate fruit; from multiple ovaries of a single flower on one receptacle
Multiple fruit; from ovaries of separate flowers clustered together
Dehiscent dry fruit; from a dry ovary wall that splits open
questions.exp: A blackberry is an aggregate fruit, developing from multiple ovaries of a single flower sharing a single receptacle.

questions.q: A pineapple develops from ovaries of separate flowers clustered together. It is classified as a:
questions.exp: Multiple fruits develop from the ovaries of several separate flowers clustered closely together.
